sm: James O'Keefe, live streaming for O'Keefe Media Group, interviews Minnesota state Representative Walter Hudson, the third lawmaker to appear in support of him. O'Keefe says Minnesota has no provisional balloting, no voter ID, and a vouching law that lets someone vouch for many people, and notes that recent races were decided by narrow margins. Hudson says he strongly backs O'Keefe and argues the charges contrast sharply with how the county prosecutor treats violent offenders. He says that as far as he can tell no law was broken, that O'Keefe took legal advice beforehand and never cast or asked for a ballot, and that the case looks frivolous and politically targeted. Hudson argues that each ballot counted from an ineligible voter disenfranchises an eligible one, and that there is no rational argument against provisional ballots. Both men say people who expose problems are being punished to send a message to others, and Hudson says he is surprised no Democratic colleagues came to oppose O'Keefe.
